source_cards.label: Theorem2.13 weighted-distance proof and the adaptive calculation preceding Eq.(4.4)
source_cards.plain: For the actual causal projected trajectory with eta_t=alpha*D/sqrt(S_(t+1)) and zero-feedback skipping, the regret is bounded by (1/(2alpha)+alpha)*D*sqrt(S_T) minus the terminal squared distance times sqrt(S_T)/(2alpha D). highlights.title: Causal adaptive OSD retains the terminal-distance residual
highlights.plain: Orabona, Online Learning: A Modern Introduction Using Convex Optimization, arXiv:1912.13213v10 (2026-06-21), printed13-14/PDF25-26 and printed39-40/PDF51-52; SHA256 cef4edfa97a6e063e53e9c532717c50aa156e5bc782ea49f969b3385011a1b17. For the actual causal projected trajectory with eta_t=alpha*D/sqrt(S_(t+1)) and zero-feedback skipping, the regret is bounded by (1/(2alpha)+alpha)*D*sqrt(S_T) minus the terminal squared distance times sqrt(S_T)/(2alpha D). The reusable potential theorem separately permits signed real a_t bounded above by C only at played indices, nonnegative nondecreasing weights and T>0; no terminal bound or lower bound on a_t is added.
highlights.intuition: For D>0, legal supporting planes and projection nonexpansiveness give the one-step distance and energy estimate. Summation by parts controls the distance terms with monotone weights sqrt(S_(t+1))/(2alpha D), retaining the signed terminal term. The shared adaptive-energy sum controls the feedback terms. Empty horizons vanish; D=0 forces feasible played and comparator points to coincide, so it is proved separately without dividing by D. Totalized real division makes the displayed residual zero at D=0.
